audit_findings.title: Historical growth may have been purchased but future acquisition spending is unfunded
audit_findings.mechanism: The 7%-9% growth assumptions compound owner earnings without deducting acquisition payments or issuing additional shares to fund acquired growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, acquisitions historically have helped significantly advance our offerings and drive growth and profitability, in both business segments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved but potentially material mismatch. Digi states that acquisitions significantly advanced growth, spent $145.702 million on Jolt in fiscal 2025 and $48.912 million on Particle during the first nine months of fiscal 2026, while the latest filing attributes most IoT Solutions growth to Jolt. Those expenditures are large relative to the $65.2 million owner-earnings anchor, but the record does not separate organic from acquired owner-earnings growth, so the recurring investment requirement cannot be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile owner-earnings growth by segment into organic and acquisition contributions, including Ventus, Jolt and Particle, then rerun the valuation using demonstrated organic growth or an explicit acquisition-investment and financing schedule.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not contain the continuing interest cost of the Jolt financing
audit_findings.magnitude: TTM interest through June 2026 was $7.886 million, $1.567 million above fiscal 2025; latest debt-rate run rate was approximately $5.396 million, $0.923 million below fiscal 2025 interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the DCF uses equity-level owner earnings, any continuing interest not represented in the anchor directly reduces projected owner earnings; debt principal is not separately deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition was funded through a combination of cash on hand and debt financing under a draw of $ 150 million from our existing credit facility committed by BMO Harris Bank N.A.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor-versus-TTM difference is demonstrated but small: $1.567 million is 2.4% of the $65.2 million anchor and would change base value by approximately $0.69 per share before tax. Moreover, June 2026 debt of $109 million at 4.95% indicates approximately $5.396 million of annual interest before fees, below fiscal 2025's $6.319 million, because substantial debt has been repaid. The evidence therefore does not establish a continuing omitted cost capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct trailing-twelve-month owner earnings through June 2026 and forecast interest from the $109 million balance, contractual rate, commitment fees and stated paydown plan; rerun only if the resulting recurring interest differs materially from the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Subscriber-equipment reinvestment can disappear between inventory and capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.793 million in fiscal 2025, $12.252 million in fiscal 2024, $3.889 million in fiscal 2023 and $5.916 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026; full fiscal-2025 omission would increase base value by approximately $3.42 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Subscriber equipment is purchased through inventory and subsequently transferred to property and equipment without appearing in reported cash capital expenditures; owner earnings is overstated if neither the working-capital calculation nor capital expenditure deduction retains that economic cost.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluded from this amount is $ 7.8 million, $ 12.3 million and $ 3.9 million of transfers of inventory to property plant and equipment for subscriber assets for the year ended September 30, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring transfers and their amounts are demonstrated, but an omission in the owner-earnings calculation is not yet demonstrated because the purchases may already reduce operating cash flow through inventory. The fiscal-2025 amount equals 12.0% of the $65.2 million anchor, and complete omission would affect base value by about 11.7%, making the accounting-path question material.
audit_findings.action: Trace subscriber-equipment purchases, inventory changes, noncash transfers, depreciation and disposals year by year; document where the cash cost enters owner earnings and rerun the DCF if it was not deducted exactly once.

audit_findings.title: A contingent-consideration liability may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid acquisition earn-out not already discharged through projected owner earnings is a senior cash claim that should reduce the equity bridge dollar for dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: Management believes that Adjusted EBITDA, defined as EBITDA adjusted for stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related expenses, restructuring charges and reversals and changes in fair value of contingent consideration is useful to investors to evaluate our core operating results and financial performance because it excludes items that are significant non-cash or non-recurring expenses reflected in the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The reported fair-value changes of negative $0.181 million in fiscal 2025 and negative $2.111 million in fiscal 2024 demonstrate that contingent consideration affected earnings, but they do not establish an outstanding settlement balance. Jolt's disclosed consideration was cash, while the latest other-liability balances are not disaggregated sufficiently to identify an earn-out. The existence and size of a bridge omission therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the September 2025 and June 2026 contingent-consideration rollforwards, acquisition agreements and other-liability detail; deduct any unpaid cash obligation not already captured in projected owner earnings and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The record anchor may capitalize a sharp margin step-up
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; fiscal-2025 gross margin rose 400 basis points to 62.9%, while fiscal-2026 nine-month and third-quarter margins were 63.8% and 64.8%
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary margin benefit embedded in the $65.2 million anchor would overstate normalized owner earnings and every subsequent growth-period cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Gross profit margin of 62.9% increased 400 basis points for fiscal 2025 as compared to the prior fiscal year.
audit_findings.explanation: The 400-basis-point fiscal-2025 increase was large, but subsequent filed results do not presently show reversal: gross margin reached 63.8% for the first nine months of fiscal 2026 and 64.8% in the third quarter, with operating margin also improving. Sustainability beyond the current product mix and acquisition period remains forward-looking, so this should be monitored rather than treated as a demonstrated anchor error.
audit_findings.action: At the fiscal-2026 10-K, compare full-year organic gross and operating margins by segment with fiscal 2025, separating Jolt, Particle, recurring-revenue mix and prior-year inventory costs; normalize and rerun only if the margin step-up reverses.

audit_findings.title: Tax benefits may make historical owner earnings a poor steady-state tax base
audit_findings.magnitude: Using the fiscal-2026 nine-month 22.6% tax rate instead of 18.3% implies approximately $2.15 million, or $0.94 per base-value share; excluding the $1.0 million discrete benefit implies approximately $3.15 million, or $1.38 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A sustainable cash-tax rate above the rate embedded in owner earnings reduces the anchor and projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective income tax expense (benefit) rates were 18.3%, 1.5% and 0.6% for fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The very low 0.6%-1.5% rates occurred in earlier years, but the valuation anchors to fiscal 2025, when the effective rate was already 18.3%. Fiscal-2026's filed nine-month rate was approximately 22.6%, or approximately 24.6% before its $1.0 million discrete benefit. Applying those differences to fiscal-2025 pretax income produces a 3.3%-4.8% anchor adjustment and approximately $0.94-$1.38 per share of base value, small relative to the $40.09 gap between the $29.27 base value and $69.36 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile owner earnings to cash taxes, separate recurring research credits from discrete benefits and deferred-tax timing, and use the resulting prospective cash-tax rate in the next scheduled rerun.
